title: APOLLAI, a multimodal AI system, versus EMS personnel for prehospital detection of stroke-related deficits
summary: In a prospective study of 295 suspected stroke patients recorded at Nîmes University Hospital, the APOLLAI multimodal AI (video and audio) was compared with EMS personnel against a seven-neurologist consensus reference for five NIHSS items. Performance was assessed by sensitivity, specificity and AUC; the abstract is cut before the final numbers.
ai_technology: APOLLAI (computer vision, audio deep learning and SVM fusion classifier)

evidence.tested: APOLLAI was evaluated prospectively on 295 patients with suspected stroke and compared with EMS personnel against an expert consensus reference.
evidence.unknown: The final sensitivity, specificity and AUC values are not in the abstract read; generalizability beyond one hospital is not stated in the reviewed material.
evidence.ai_role: A multimodal machine-learning system detected stroke-related neurological deficits from video and audio recordings and was compared with clinicians' assessments.
